---
title: "Where to go next"
subtitle: "Courses and books, checked against their official pages"
---

Each entry was checked on its official page or publisher record; the dates are the most
recent offering listed there.

## Books {#books}

- **Sutton and Barto, *Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction*, 2nd edition** [@sutton2018rl]. The free online edition is the course's backbone for Days 1–4.
- **Lattimore and Szepesvári, *Bandit Algorithms*** [@lattimore2020bandit]. The reference for Day 2: concentration (Ch. 5), UCB (Ch. 7), linear bandits (Ch. 19–20), Thompson sampling (Ch. 36).
- **Agarwal, Jiang, Kakade and Sun, *Reinforcement Learning: Theory and Algorithms*** [@agarwal2022rltheory]. The theory behind Days 1 and 4, if you want the proofs.
- **Szepesvári, *Algorithms for Reinforcement Learning*** [@szepesvari2010algorithms]. A compact algorithmic survey.

## Courses {#courses}

- **UC Berkeley CS 185/285, Deep Reinforcement Learning** (Sergey Levine) [@levine2026cs285].
- **Stanford CS234, Reinforcement Learning** (Emma Brunskill) [@brunskill2026cs234].
- **Stanford CS 224R, Deep Reinforcement Learning** (Chelsea Finn) [@finn2026cs224r].
- **CMU 10-703, Deep Reinforcement Learning** (Fall 2026: Katerina Fragkiadaki and Max Simchowitz) [@cmu2026deeprl].
- **MIT 6.7920, Reinforcement Learning: Foundations and Methods** (Cathy Wu and Munther Dahleh) [@wu2026mit6792].
- **DeepMind x UCL Reinforcement Learning Lecture Series, 2021** [@vanhasselt2021ucl], and **David Silver's UCL course, 2015** [@silver2015ucl].
- **OpenAI Spinning Up in Deep RL** [@achiam2018spinningup] (in maintenance) and the **Hugging Face Deep RL Course** [@simonini2023hfdeeprl] (low-maintenance).

## Topics this workshop leaves out {#out-of-scope}

Heavy theory, robotics simulators, distributed RL infrastructure, continuous-time control,
Monte Carlo tree search and AlphaZero, and language-model pretraining. Annotated pointers for
each are added in Phase 4, once each source has been checked.
